title: Sample 15-2: Prose Numbered Every Ten Lines

illustrates.quote: 15.4.1 Prose is ordinary speech or writing without rhyme or meter. Observe the following guidelines, in addition to the points outlined in Formats, §15.3: a. Follow print for indented or blocked paragraphing. b. Every print line of prose is numbered in braille, even when the lines are not numbered in print. c. Three blank cells precede a new print line when it begins in the middle of a braille line. Do not insert three blank cells before a new print line when it begins a new braille line.

Both A and B already agreed on this file's wording and braille; this reconciliation's only change is populating the ten intervening numbers instead of leaving them null, so buildModel15 exercises per-line prose numbering (not just the two print-visible anchors).

braille.notes: CORRECTED during reconciliation: both A and B's own line text was byte-identical to the source's raw text extraction, but that raw extraction right-justifies every number far past column 40 (lines up to 66 characters long) even though this file's own declared braille.width is 40 and every other file in this section right-justifies its own numbers at exactly column 40. Re-derived directly: with this passage's widest number '#bij'/290 (4 cells) and the wrapNumbered algorithm's own 2-blank-cell minimum, the correct gap is exactly `40 - textLength - 4`, which the ORIGINAL extraction overshoots by roughly 26 extra blank cells on every numbered row — a text-extraction artifact (the source PDF's copyable text layer apparently right-justifies these rows against the page's own physical margin, not the 40-cell braille measure), not a genuine part of the braille. Each line's own text and number are unchanged; only the padding was reduced so every numbered line is exactly 40 cells. Right-margin numbers 279-290 confirmed sequential by direct decode of every '#[a-j]+' token in this array.

resolution: Braille: A and B agreed on every character but both preserved a raw text-extraction artifact (numbers right-justified far past the declared 40-cell width); re-justified to column 40 during this reconciliation (see braille.notes). Print side: both runs agreed on wording and the two print-visible anchors (280, 290); this reconciliation adds the ten intervening sequential numbers, decoded directly from the gold braille's own right-margin digits, matching what 15.4.1b actually requires. Modeled by buildModel15 as ONE flowing numbered paragraph per print paragraph (both marked 'newPara'), with a genuine linenum segment before each print line's own text, feeding Emboss's wrapNumbered mechanism — per the standards-findings.md 'done' rows for 15.3-15.4 (wrapNumbered's own right-margin/three-blank-cell behaviour is not itself defective), this file is expected to be among the section's few genuine MATCHes.
